observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a polished wooden floor, a full-width mirror wall fronted by a horizontal ballet barre, frosted-glass panels on either side, a row of clerestory windows at the top, and a round wall clock on the right. A man in a black sleeveless shirt bearing a pink-and-yellow chest logo, black trousers and multicoloured sneakers occupies the centre, his back initially to the camera; his front is seen in the mirror. The mirror also reflects other participants standing in the room behind the camera (a person in a teal top and purple trousers to the left, a person in a yellow top to the right, and seated figures further left). The camera viewpoint is fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The central man rotates his torso and shifts his arm poses continuously: arms extended sideways (frames 1-2), body turning to a right-side profile with arms bent in front (frames 3-5), then facing the camera with arms opened wide to the sides (frames 6-9, head turned to his left in 8-9), turning back to profile with arms crossed/bent (frames 10-12), and returning to a back-to-camera stance with arms out (frames 13-16).
His feet change stance: a left foot lifts and crosses during the turn (frames 3-5), and the legs reposition through the rotation (frames 10-15).
Arms draw in toward the chest (frames 17-19), then hands rest on the hips (frames 20-21), then drop to the sides.
A prolonged near-static interval occurs (frames 22-33): the man stands with his back to the camera, legs apart, arms hanging at his sides, with only minimal postural sway.
After the pause the arms lift outward again into a wide horizontal 'T'-like pose (frames 34-39), then bend back in toward the front (frames 40-41).

The mirror image tracks the man's orientation, showing his front when he faces the mirror and his back when he turns away; the reflected background participants remain largely in place with only small movements.
Background elements (clock, panels, barre, floor, other reflected people) show no change in position, indicating the camera is stationary rather than panning.
outside_clip_unknowns: The start and end of the choreography and any musical cue are outside the segment; the first and last poses are arbitrary crop boundaries, not a completed move.
Whether the reflected people are following the same routine is not determinable from these frames.
The reason for the mid-segment standing pause is not visible.
uncertain_details: Exact footwork during the turns is partly obscured by the body and the barre line.
Tiny shifts in the reflected participants' arm positions are hard to confirm against the static mirror frame.
Subtle weight shifts during the static interval (frames 22-33) are minimal and may be imperceptible sway rather than deliberate motion.
